Area.evidence_source: Alcohol is known to increase the chances of a lethal effect of other substances (Stack & Wasserman, 1993). This might have been the motivation for some of the decedents as the quote below appears to suggest: . . . the boy went to the shop, bought waragi [local spirit] and yet he never used to drink alcohol and also bought sibacon and a battery cell, went down to [an isolated place] that side of the borehole, mixed those items and drunk. (case12:informant1) This informant seems to suggest that the person purposely bought alcohol to mix it with organophosphate and the watch cell powder in order to achieve a maximum lethal effect. This indicates how determined this person was to end his life; he made sure he minimized all chances of being rescued. It is most likely that the mixing of alcohol with other lethal substances meant the decedents were really determined to die and had no trust in a single substance achieving what they desired. In the above quote the deceased mixed alcohol with organophosphates and watch cell; others mixed alcohol with organophosphates and one dissolved chloroquine tablets in alcohol.
